description.narrative:
The aim of project is to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of interisland shipping services through provision of an integrated package of assistance. It comprises two major components:
(a) infrastructure investments in the capital of Port Vila and five outer islands, and
(b) establishment of a shipping support scheme to catalyze the provision of services to remote noncommercial destinations using an output-based aid approach.
The Project is complemented by associated TA to improve sector governance through institutional strengthening and legal and regulatory reforms, and by project management services.

Output: Shipping support and coordination schemes have been established Indicator: Shipping services provided to project areas Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Shipping services to Tafea East, Tafea West, Torres, Santo, and Banks have been identified under the SSS component. All contracts were awarded by July 2021 and these shipping services became operational. However, in February 2022, Santo route contract was terminated and the government no longer intends to rebid the package for this route considering that the worth of the contract is very low compared to the current cost escalation due to the impact of coronavirus disease and the ongoing global increase in fuel prices. Output: Improved maritime infrastructure is provided in the capital and rural areas Indicator: Construction is complete in Port Vila with a dredged channel Achievement: 1 Progress/Status: Redesigning of all five wharves under the project is already completed (South Paray, Simonsen, Port Sandwich, Lenakel, and Litzlitz). Designs were verified by independent international design reviewer firm.
Lenakel and Litzlitz wharves contract was awarded on 26 July 2021 and repair works completed in June and July 2022, respectively.
South Paray wharf contract was awarded on 16 June 2022 with construction time of 2 years and expected completion of civil works has been extended to Q2 2025 due to the impact of the two tropical cyclones that hit the country in 2023 adn the earthquake that his Port Vila in December 2024.
Package for Port Sandwich and Simonsen is no longer pushing through under this project due to financing gap. Bids for remaining two wharves opened on 31 Aug 2022 with almost 100% cost overrun against engineer's estimate. Procurement activities stopped at price negotiations stage in Q2 2023. Government will arrange to cover any financing gap under the project. NZ MFAT grant is also financing the remaining works for South Paray. South Paray wharf was completed in Q2 2025. A soft launch was facilitated by the government in April 2025.
Project team has initiated the processing of a minor change to remove the unfunded small wharves from the project scope. However, Port Vila was hit by an earthquake on 17 Dec 2024 and hence, VPMU was not able to provide its response and confirmation. During the review mission fielded on 10-14 Mar 2025, ADB project team reminded VPMU and MIPU on the proposed minor change in scope. On 20 May 2025, VPMU submitted to ADB, MIPU's official request for minor change. As of end Q2 2025, the DMF-related minor change memo has been under review by supporting departments as part of due diligence and is expected to be approved by July 2025 to be followed by amendments to loans' agreements. Data Source: Quarterly reports from project steering committee

Main population centers in project areas receive a vessel call at least once every two months Achievement: 6 Progress/Status: The SSS component under the project has awarded all contracts by July 2021 with 194.5 voyages completed as of 15 October 2024. The main population centers in route areas received a monthly shipping service. But after the twin cyclones (Kevin and Judy) in 2023, the schedule became irregular due to bad weather conditions. Humanitarian aid relief supplies chartered by the nominated vessel, as well as various mechanical breakdowns of the nominated vessel have also impacted the service schedule. Data Source: Maritime regulatory authority reports

All vessels in Vanuatu comply with national safety regulations Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: The Office of Maritime Regulator was established in July 2017 and the Regulator was appointed in July 2010. Additional support has been provided by ADB to assist in the implementation of reforms and strengthening of the OMR. The Government has provided resources and budget for its operations, but OMR needs further support in strengthening their policy and sustainability of its operations as a regulator. The government is in process of change in legislation to bring all ports and wharfs in country under Department of Ports and Marine (DPM). The government will provide budget support to DPM for its operations and maintenance. The amendment in act was passed by Parliament in 2021. During review mission in February 2023, project team was informed that OMR has merged into a newly created entity, the Vanuatu Maritime Safety Authority in 2022. Data Source: Maritime regulatory authority reports

Sailing schedules to all islands are published and 90% of vessel calls are delivered without cancellations or delays greater than 24 hours Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: Only shipping support scheme schedules are being published. Shipping support scheme voyage reports are analyzed and reported in quarterly progress report. As of 15 October 2024, 194.5 voyages are completed with a total of 2,747 passengers out of which 1,837 are male and 910 are female; and with a total of 4,312.57 tons and 9,439.66 cubic meters cargoes.
